chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā; and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: concerning
a well into which a child urinates, or urine is poured into it, or wine; so he said: “All of the water is to be drawn out.”

So what this report includes of mentioning the urine of a child or the pouring of urine into it is to be understood as applying when the taste or smell of the water has changed, because whenever the water has not changed, then it has a specified amount that is to be drawn from it, and we shall mention it later, if Allah the Exalted wills.

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: a child whose urine is mentioned as a source of contamination
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine as a najis substance affecting the well water
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, mentioned here as an impurity falling into the well
key_terms.رَائِحَتُهُ: its smell, whose change indicates the ruling for full removal
key_terms.طَعْمُ: the taste of the water, whose change indicates contamination
key_terms.قَدْرًا مُقَدَّرًا: a specified measured amount to be drawn when the water itself has not changed
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: is to be drawn out, meaning water must be removed from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if urine or wine falls into it?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a well contaminated by a child’s urine, urine poured into it, or wine. It states that all the water should be drawn out, then clarifies that this applies when the water’s taste or smell has changed; otherwise, a fixed amount is to be removed.
